content.title: HITMAN
content.description: Sample model for the picker. Scroll-driven 3D showcase.

sections.name: Intro
sections.kicker: Demo asset // nobody real signed off on this
sections.heading: HIT|MAN
sections.body: A generated stand-in, kept around so this site ships with two models instead of one. Point the studio at it, publish it, tune a camera path on it, throw it away. It exists to be swapped out — which is the same thing your own product will do to it.

sections.name: Profile
sections.heading:
This was supposed
to be a backpack
sections.body: One word in the brief. Backpacker. What came out is a tactical harness with two heraldic crests that have never appeared on any backpack ever manufactured by anyone. And here is the part that bothers me — it looks better. Five seconds of compute out-designed the brief.

sections.name: Works
sections.heading:
Nobody asked
for a gun
sections.body: It just showed up. A man in a suit was described and the machine decided he needed to be armed. Which — fine — is actually the pitch. This stop is a product slot. Swap the .glb, move one line of keyframe, and the camera orbits a perfume bottle with exactly the same reverence it is currently giving a weapon nobody ordered.

sections.name: Contact
sections.heading:
Only the shoes
came out right
sections.body: Three hundred thousand polygons of disappointment, and then — shoes. Clean welt, correct specular, actual laces. If you own a product that genuinely exists, this gets embarrassingly good. Details below. Use them or do not.
